title: per-tenant-kms-subkey-scoping-and-audit-derivative-index
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce tenant-scoped derived KMS subkeys for improved key separation plus an audit derivative index for fast duplicate-detection in audit pipelines. Backfill/migration tool included; rollout gated behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: multi-tenant customers and compliance reviewers requested stronger cryptographic separation without proliferating CMKs. This PR introduces tenant-scoped derived subkeys (HKDF-derived AES-GCM wrapping keys anchored to an existing CMK) and a compact audit derivative index to allow fast deduplication and integrity checks in the audit pipeline.

What this PR does: 1) KMS allocator: derive per-tenant subkeys from a root CMK using HKDF with tenant and service namespace as info; derivation is deterministic so no extra storage for subkeys is required. 2) Enforcement shim: runtime checks that ensures requests with tenant-scoped key material are tagged and routed to region-anchored CMKs (region pinning) and fail closed when mismatch detected. 3) Audit pipeline: a new derivative index component computes a stable fingerprint on relevant request metadata + wrapped ciphertext and stores a compact (BLAKE2b-128) fingerprint in the audit index to enable efficient duplicate-detection and compact retention policies. 4) Migration/backfill: a post-deploy backfill tool (opt-in) that can compute derivative fingerprints for historical audit entries and populate the index in a controlled, throttled way. 5) Feature flags + rollout: flags added for derivation-enabled and audit-index-enabled to allow gradual rollout per-tenant and per-region.

Compatibility and safety: the derived subkeys do not replace CMKs; they are used solely for envelope wrapping in the platform so external customer CMK workflows are unaffected. The derivation uses the same CMK for signing the derivation label (HMAC) to provide non-repudiation. All code paths include fallbacks to the previous behavior when feature flags are off.

Operational notes and migration: - Default: feature flags off for all tenants. Engage with Security/GTM for tenant opt-ins. - Backfill tool supports batch windowing and rate limits. Backfill can run against a read-replica to avoid contention. - We add metrics: kms.derived_subkey.requests, kms.derived_subkey.failures, audit.index.ingest_rate, audit.index.backfill_progress.

Testing and CI: unit tests for derivation and policy checks, integration tests for audit pipeline (local in-memory index), and an end-to-end smoke test exercising the feature-flagged path. Load tests show ~2% extra CPU on the KMS proxy pod under 1k rps due to HMAC operations; we included micro-optimizations to reuse HKDF state across batch operations.

Security review: design reviewed by Security (SEC-88). Threat model updates included in the PR attachments. No plaintext key material is logged or persisted.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind flags. 2) Enable derivation for a small internal tenant and run backfill with low concurrency. 3) Monitor metrics and audit-index false-positive rate for one week. 4) Gradually expand.

Rollback: flip feature flags off (immediate), purge newly created index entries via backfill control plane if needed, and revoke derived-key usage by refusing derived-wrapped tokens at the policy layer.

Notes: this approach was chosen over creating explicit per-tenant CMKs for cost and management reasons; it still satisfies most compliance patterns because the derivation is bound to tenant identity and CMK provenance (region awareness).

review_comments: Diego Chen: Strong idea. Two asks: (1) show explicit non-replayability guarantees in the doc (tie derivation label to request nonce or timestamp), (2) can we use BLAKE2b-128 instead of SHA256 for index to reduce storage?

Priya Nair (author): Reply: added nonce binding to derivation label and switched to BLAKE2b-128 for fingerprinting; updated docs and tests. Backfill uses timestamp windows to prevent replay amplification.
Ravi Patel: Please add a rate limit guard on the backfill worker and a circuit-breaker for the audit index ingestion to handle spikes. Also request a short-lived feature flag for immediate rollback.
Priya Nair: Added token-bucket rate limiter to backfill worker and an ingestion queue depth metric. Short-lived rollback flag added with higher priority. Updated helm values to expose thresholds.
Emma Lawson: Code review minor: prefer context timeouts in allocator.go and small naming nit. Approved after fixes.
CI bot: integration tests initially failed on audit index concurrency; issue fixed by queue sizing change and tests rerun. All checks passed.
Security (SEC-88): Reviewed threat model; acceptable with controls. Recommend a quarterly key-usage attestation for tenanted derivations.
